title: Signal-driven catalog intake, SLA prioritization, and safe pin/deprecation pathways
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request new model additions, version pins, or scheduled deprecations with asymmetric urgency and compliance constraints. Current intake is ad hoc and routes requests to multiple teams, which causes slow turnarounds, missed SLAs, and risky simultaneous deprecations. Goal: Define a signal-driven intake protocol that maps incoming requests to SLA buckets, applies automated and human eval gates, and produces a deterministic safe-path for pinning and deprecation that minimizes customer disruption while meeting security and compliance policies.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented intake rubric that converts request signals into one of three SLA buckets (Expedite: 3 business days, Standard: 15 business days, Low: 45 business days).

A2: Automated evaluation pipeline triggers for newly proposed models and version pins that run a defined minimal eval suite (latency, token-efficiency, safety checks, dataset overlap) and returns a pass/fail + score within 24 hours for Expedite and 72 hours for Standard buckets.

A3: Defined pin workflow with explicit fallback policies: when a customer requests a pin, the catalog must record the pin, route telemetry alerts, and provide an automated rollback trigger if regression or outage occurs.
A4: Deprecation schedule template with staggered notification windows (30/14/7 days) and an emergency hold mechanism that can pause deprecation within 48 hours of customer impact evidence.
A5: Stakeholder approval matrix showing which requests require security review, legal review, or executive sign-off (implemented as tags in intake form).
A6: Dashboards showing queue size by SLA bucket, average lead time, eval pass rates, and active pins with owner and expiration.
implementation_notes: Intake signals to capture: customer tier (gold/silver/self-serve), request type (new-model, pin, deprecate), business rationale, data residency constraints, eval dataset suggestions, desired TTL for pin, and rollback tolerance.
Scoring rubric proposal: weighted scores across Production Readiness (40%), Cost Impact (20%), Security/Compliance (20%), Customer Criticality (20%). Use thresholds to push to expedited review.

Automated eval suite minimum: throughput benchmark (tokens/sec), 95th pct latency for typical prompt set, toxicity/safety classifier pass, simple hallucination regression on canonical prompts, embedding similarity overlap check against customer-sensitive datasets.
Telemetry hooks: require a lightweight SDK event to appear in runtime telemetry for any pinned model so SRE can surface anomalies and initiate rollback within policy.
Integrations: Confluence for playbook, GitHub actions to kick eval runs, Datadog/Grafana for dashboards, Jira/GH issues for tracking longer work, and Slack channel for expedite approvals.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): Run protocol for three enterprise customers known to request pins frequently. Validate automated eval runtime and dashboard signals. (2 sprints)
Phase 1: Open protocol to all enterprise accounts with dedicated intake form. Train Solutions Engineering and Customer Success on the rubric. (1 month)
Phase 2: Expose opt-in self-serve for standard/low bucket requests in Console UI; enforce expedite path for gold-tier customers via API flags. (2 months)
Phase 3: Iterate on thresholds and automated evals after 6 weeks of telemetry; bake into SLA docs and support contracts.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated eval false negatives allow poor models into pinned production. Mitigation: conservative thresholds for expedite bucket and mandatory human review for security score < 0.8.
Risk: Deprecation notices insufficiently reach downstream teams. Mitigation: enforce required stakeholder list on intake and integrate with Customer Success notification playbook.
Risk: Increased operational load on SRE from pinned-model telemetry. Mitigation: cap number of active pins per customer by default and add quota enforcement during rollout.
next_steps: 1) Draft the intake form fields and scoring weights and circulate to Security, SRE, and Solutions Engineering for comment by 2025-02-22.
2) ENG to prototype a minimal eval pipeline (ENG-8423) and expose a pass/fail API by 2025-03-07.
3) Build dashboard mockups and run pilot with two customers in March.
4) Confirm legal and compliance notification triggers and finalize sign-off matrix.
